newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police arrest Islamist protesters.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police arrest Islamist protesters.

text.p: Turkish police on Friday detained at least 20 people at a rowdy Islamist demonstration against government plans to curb Moslem religious education, witnesses said.
"You can't stop the Islamic movement," hundreds of protesters chanted outside the 16th-century Beyazit mosque after noon prayers.

Police with helmets and plastic body armour -- known locally as "robocops" -- broke up the protest and chased the Islamists up sidestreets. Two police minibuses later took detainees away from the area.
Minor clashes broke out between small groups of protesters and police in the nearby Fatih district as the crowds dispersed.
One woman wearing a mini-skirt was detained by police after being involved in a tussle with bearded Islamist protesters.
Security had been tight at large mosques throughout Turkey following a demonstration in Ankara earlier in the week that turned ugly.

Eleven people, mostly journalists, were wounded on Tuesday when police baton-charged thousands of Islamists in the capital protesting at a goverment bid to extend secularist education at the expense of Islamic secondary schools.
Police commanders were heard to shout "No batons, no batons," in an effort to calm junior officers as they chased the fleeing protesters on Friday.
Police searched worshippers at many major mosques as they arrived for Friday prayers, the holiest point in the Moslem week.
Uniformed and plainclothes police milled around the Grand Mosque in Diyarbakir, the main city in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
Islamist anger at Turkey's secularist establishment has risen since Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned under military pressure in June. He was replaced by secularist Mesut Yilmaz.
Senior Islamist politician Oguzhan Asilturk told reporters it was only Erbakan's Welfare Party which could stop the tension turning into violence.
"Without Welfare there is no force to prevent the provocations turning into rivers of blood. We are preventing this," Asilturk told a news conference in Ankara.
A car bomb exploded in central Turkey on Friday in an apparent attempt to free eight Islamist convicts being carried to court in an armoured prison vehicle, Anatolian news agency said.
It said three gendarmerie police and an inmate were wounded in the attack in Kirsehir province.
